G: The finite connected undirected graph in the theorem statement.
P: a trail in G having the maximum possible number of edges
x: A vertex occurring on C that is incident with an edge not used by C.
C: A closed trail in G chosen to have the largest possible number of edges.
H: The spanning subgraph of G consisting exactly of the edges not used by C.
D: A nonempty closed trail in H starting and ending at x.
s: A chosen starting vertex incident with at least one edge.
t: The terminal vertex of a maximal greedily extended trail.
y: An arbitrary vertex used when checking residual degree parity.
edge-incidence: one occurrence of an edge at an endpoint, with a loop contributing two incidences
residual degree: the degree of a vertex in H
T: a trail of G with the largest possible number of edges
k: the positive integer equal to the number of edges of T
v_i: the vertex in position i of the traversal T
e_i: the edge in position i of the traversal T
V(T): the set of vertices that occur in T
f: an edge of G not used by T and incident with x
g: an edge of G not in T and incident with a vertex of T
w: a vertex of S incident with f
m: the number of edges of T
S: the set of all vertices occurring on T
i: an integer index satisfying 0<=i<m for an occurrence v_i=x
u: An endpoint of an edge of G not used by C.
trail: A walk that repeats no edge.
closed trail: A trail whose initial and terminal vertices coincide.
edge-end: One incidence of an edge with a vertex; a loop has two edge-ends at its vertex.
